name: Luxembourg
tagline: One small multilingual university, and a semester abroad built in
summary: Luxembourg has essentially one public university, founded in 2003, and it is unlike anywhere else on this site. Programmes are multilingual by design - many bachelor's are taught in two languages, typically French and English or French and German - and every bachelor student has to spend a semester abroad, which is written into the rules rather than offered as an option. It is small, well funded, and sits at the centre of EU institutions and international finance. The country is also one of the most expensive in Europe to live in, and there is only one annual intake, in September.
whyConsider: Very low public tuition compared with anywhere outside continental Europe, and the same fee whether you are EU or not.
A compulsory semester abroad in every bachelor's degree, so international mobility is guaranteed rather than something you have to organise.
Multilingualism is the point: if you have IB French B or German B alongside English, Luxembourg turns that into an asset rather than a hurdle.
Small cohorts and close contact with staff at a university of a few thousand students.
Location. The Court of Justice of the EU, the European Investment Bank, Eurostat and a large financial sector are all in the same city, which matters for law, economics and finance internships.
watchOuts: English alone is often not enough. Many bachelor's require French or German as well as English, and the requirement is per programme. Read the language requirements of the individual programme before anything else.

One intake a year, in September, with no spring or summer entry. Applications for 2027-2028 open on 1 February 2027, and the university has said the admission criteria for that year are under review and may change.

Every programme sets its own closing date and they are not the same. In the 2026-2027 cycle Computer Science closed for EU applicants on 15 July and a second programme was indexed as closing on 8 July. Read your own programme’s admissions page rather than any university-wide date, including the ones on this page.
Very small choice. This is one university with a limited range of bachelor's - if your subject is not among them, Luxembourg is simply not an option.
Cost of living is high. Rents in and around Luxembourg City are among the most expensive in the EU, and student housing is limited.
The compulsory mobility semester is a real constraint if you have family or work commitments; waivers exist but are not automatic.

Two private schools often listed for Luxembourg are not options. Sacred Heart University closed its Luxembourg campus in 2022 and shu.lu is now a parked domain; BBI hospitality school’s address, bbi-edu.eu, now serves an unrelated gambling page. Neither appears on the ministry’s list of accredited specialised institutions, which names only LUNEX and the Luxembourg School of Business.

ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: The University of Luxembourg assesses foreign school-leaving diplomas individually against its programme-specific admission criteria, and states that the criteria for 2027-2028 are under review. No IB-specific rule is published. The decisive requirement in practice is the language combination the programme demands, not a points threshold.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: No official IB-to-Luxembourgish conversion is published.
notes: A full IB Diploma is a university-entrance qualification recognised across the EU, and Luxembourg admits students from a very wide range of national systems - but confirm your specific case with the university's student department (SEVE) rather than assuming.
If you plan to have your degree formally recognised in Luxembourg later, Luxembourg maintains a Register of Titles (registre des titres) for higher education qualifications.
Because the university says its admission criteria for 2027-2028 are under review, treat everything here as provisional and re-read the university's admissions pages in late 2026.

deadlines.label: Applications open for the 2027-2028 academic year
deadlines.year: 2027-2028 entry - stated on the university’s own admissions page
deadlines.notes: On 23 September 2026 the university's admissions page said: "The application period for the 2026–2027 academic year is now closed. Applications for the 2027–2028 academic year will open on 1 February 2027." The university offers one intake a year, in September, and states there are no spring or summer intakes. The same page warns that "The application criteria for the 2027–2028 academic year are currently under review and may be subject to change", so the eligibility rules you plan around today may not be the ones you apply under. There is an application fee, paid as step five of the application, before you can submit.

deadlines.label: Closing date for bachelor applications - set per programme, not once for the university
deadlines.year: 2027-2028 entry - the 2027-2028 closing dates were not published on 2026-09-23
deadlines.notes: There is no single University of Luxembourg deadline: each programme publishes its own, on its own admissions page, and they differ by more than a week. Precedent, from the Bachelor in Computer Science admissions page on 23 September 2026: "EU: 1 Feb 2026 – 15 Jul 2026". That is nine days after IB results are released, so an EU student could apply on actual results rather than predicted ones. Do not generalise it, though: a date of 8 July 2026 circulates for the Bachelor en Medecine, but it is not on the university's own page, so do not rely on it. Take the date from your own programme’s admissions page, and take it early.

deadlines.label: Closing date for bachelor applications, the much earlier non-EU window
deadlines.year: 2027-2028 entry - the 2027-2028 closing dates were not published on 2026-09-23
deadlines.audience: applicants who are not EU citizens
deadlines.notes: Precedent, from the Bachelor in Computer Science admissions page on 23 September 2026: "Non-EU: 1 Feb 2026 – 24 Mar 2026" - nearly four months earlier than the EU window, and three and a half months before IB results exist. The same 24 March appeared for a second programme. If you are not an EU citizen, Luxembourg is a predicted-grades application and the July advantage that EU applicants get does not exist for you.

deadlines.label: The application window and the enrolment window - the university and the state portal do not describe the same period
deadlines.notes: Two official Luxembourgish pages describe the period for getting into the University of Luxembourg and they do not agree, so no single window is recorded here. The university’s own admissions page says applications for 2027-2028 "will open on 1 February 2027", and its programme pages give windows running from 1 February to July. The state portal guichet.public.lu, on its page "Enrolling at the University of Luxembourg", says enrolment runs "from the end of April to mid-September" for a bachelor. Both were read on 23 September 2026 and both are live. The likeliest explanation is that guichet is describing enrolment after admission while the university is describing application - but guichet’s page is headed "This page is currently being updated", which is the publisher telling you it may be stale. What to do instead: work to the dates on your own programme’s page at uni.lu, and if the guichet window is the one you were counting on, get it confirmed by the university’s student department (SEVE) before you rely on it.

steps: Choose a programme from the university's bachelor list and read its language requirements first - this is what decides whether Luxembourg is viable for you.
Check the eligibility criteria for that programme, and note that the university says its 2027-2028 criteria are under review.
Prepare your documents: IB transcript or predicted grades, school-leaving certificate, proof of the required languages, passport, motivation letter.

Create an account on the university’s admission platform when applications open on 1 February 2027, and find your own programme’s closing date on its admissions page - there is no single university-wide deadline.
Complete the application and pay the application fee, then submit online.
If admitted, enrol and pay the semester registration fee, and start looking for accommodation immediately - housing is the tightest constraint in Luxembourg.
Plan for the compulsory semester abroad, normally taken in the third, fourth or fifth semester.
application.selectionNotes: Admission is decided by the university programme by programme against published eligibility criteria, rather than by a national points system or a central office. There is no numerus fixus system of the Dutch kind and no CAO-style ranking; the practical filters are the language combination and the subject prerequisites of the individual programme.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Small and mostly multilingual rather than purely English. The University of Luxembourg builds bachelor's around combinations of French, English and German, so a programme described as partly English-taught may still require French or German for a substantial part of the teaching. A few programmes are taught wholly in English. No count of fully English-taught bachelor programmes is confirmed here.
language.englishProof: Set per programme by the University of Luxembourg; no national rule. An IB Diploma taken in English will usually satisfy the English component, but you must check whether the programme also requires French or German and at what level.
notes: Luxembourgish is the national language, with French and German as administrative languages. You will not normally need Luxembourgish to study, but French is genuinely useful for daily life, administration and student jobs.
If you took French B or German B in the IB, say so in your application - the multilingual profile is exactly what this university is built around.
Luxembourg also runs BTS programmes (two-year higher technician diplomas) in its secondary schools, taught mainly in French; these are a different route from a university bachelor's.

tuitionEuEea.value: Registration fee of 400 EUR per semester at the University of Luxembourg; the university notes that fees may vary by programme, so check your programme page.
tuitionEuEea.year: Current figure on the university budget page, read 2026-09-24

tuitionNonEu.value: The university budget page gives the same 400 EUR per semester and does not distinguish by nationality; check your programme page.
tuitionNonEu.year: Current figure on the university budget page, read 2026-09-24

livingCostMonthly.value: At least 1,517 EUR a month (18,211 EUR per academic year): the resources the immigration authority requires, which the University of Luxembourg quotes as its budget floor. University housing starts at 450 EUR a month and is not guaranteed; private rooms cost significantly more. Plan about 2,700 EUR for the first weeks (registration, insurance, first rent and deposit).
livingCostMonthly.year: 2025 figure, as published by the University of Luxembourg

notes: University of Luxembourg registration is charged per semester (400 EUR on the university budget page, read 2026-09-24). Fees may vary by programme.

There is an application fee, and paying it is step five of the application process on the university's own admissions page, so you cannot submit without it. The current amount is not confirmed here: the university's 2022 news item is titled "Uni.lu introduces a 50 EUR application fee". Check the amount before budgeting.
Luxembourg has one of the highest costs of living in the EU, driven mainly by rent. Public transport inside the country is free.

funding.note: It can follow you to a full degree here if the programme is SU-approved; outside the Nordics it is capped at four years (48 klip). Apply to Uddannelses- og Forskningsstyrelsen before you leave.

funding: Luxembourg state financial aid for higher education (AideFi, the successor to CEDIES aid) exists in the form of grants and loans, and is administered through guichet.public.lu. It is aimed at residents and at the children of people working in Luxembourg; the exact eligibility conditions for a newly arrived EU student are not confirmed here, so check them at guichet.public.lu before assuming you qualify.
Erasmus+ funding is available for the compulsory mobility semester, which reduces its cost.
Student jobs exist in Luxembourg City and pay comparatively well, but often expect French and sometimes Luxembourgish.
workRights: As an EU citizen you may work in Luxembourg without a permit. A student enrolled in Luxembourg can work on a student fixed-term contract for up to 15 hours a week on average over a month (60 hours) during term, and up to the normal 40 hours a week in the holidays, at no less than the age-adjusted minimum wage (guichet.public.lu).
residency: As an EU citizen you enter with your EU passport or national ID card and need no visa. You must make a declaration of arrival at the commune where you live, and after three months register as an EU citizen residing in Luxembourg, showing proof of enrolment, sufficient resources and health cover. Non-EU students need a temporary authorisation to stay before travelling, followed by a residence permit after arrival.
housing: The hardest practical problem of studying in Luxembourg. The country has one of the most expensive rental markets in the EU and the student population competes with a large professional and cross-border workforce. The University of Luxembourg runs its own student housing service and this should be your first and main approach - apply as soon as you are admitted, not after. If you miss university housing, consider living just across the border in France, Germany or Belgium and commuting: public transport inside Luxembourg is free, and many students in the Greater Region do exactly this. No official rent figures are quoted here.
healthcare: Bring your European Health Insurance Card from the country where you are insured. If you register as a resident and study in Luxembourg for a full degree, you will normally be affiliated to the Luxembourg health insurance system (CNS) - the university's student department explains the process during enrolment. Non-EU students must show proof of health cover to obtain their residence permit.

institutions.name: University of Luxembourg
institutions.englishBachelors: A small multilingual bachelor portfolio; several programmes involve English alongside French or German
institutions.note: The country's only public university, built on a redeveloped steelworks site at Belval, with a compulsory semester abroad in every bachelor's degree.

institutions.name: LUNEX University
institutions.englishBachelors: English-taught bachelor's in physiotherapy, osteopathy, sport and exercise science, international sport management, and nutrition, fitness and health
institutions.note: A private, fully English-taught health and sport university - the most straightforward English-language bachelor route in Luxembourg, but it charges private tuition.
